pathAssistantSteps.info: Record the initial research finding or scientific principle that may have practical value. Capture the researchers, supporting publications or data, and the problem the discovery could address.
Define the proposed technology and its potential application. Confirm the researcher can explain how the concept would work, who may benefit, and what evidence is needed next.

Document proof-of-concept results showing that the core idea can work. Review the evidence, identify any new intellectual property, and note the main technical and market assumptions still to be tested.
Confirm that the main components work together in a controlled research setting. Record prototype results, limitations, ownership and funding obligations, and any protection or disclosure deadlines.

Validate the technology under conditions that reflect its intended use. Capture feedback from prospective users or industry partners, compare performance with alternatives, and define the work needed for a pilot.

Demonstrate an integrated prototype in a relevant setting with credible users or partners. Document performance, reproducibility, regulatory considerations, partner interest, and the development plan for adoption or licensing.

Run a full prototype in the intended operating environment. Confirm that it meets user requirements and agree the remaining technical, regulatory, manufacturing, funding, and commercial steps with the development partner.

Confirm the technology is complete and has passed the required qualification, compliance, and acceptance testing. Finalize the evidence and agreements needed for launch, deployment, or transfer to the licensee or spinout.

Record evidence that the technology is performing successfully in routine use. Track adoption, licensee or spinout milestones, income and impact, and any further intellectual property or research opportunities.
